method.weights: core.StatWeights of the engine: the metric per one unit of the stat, the mean of paired differences against the baseline at the same seeds, from a run above the baseline and, except for hit and expertise, one below it. step is the size of that run.
method.ep: ep is the weight divided by the weight of the tree's reference stat, with its sign kept: a negative ep is a stat that moves the metric against the reference stat. In tank.dtps and tank.tmi it divides by the weight of StatArmor, so a positive ep there lowers damage taken as armor does. The engine's own EP values are absolute and are not used.
method.interval: stdev is the standard deviation of the paired differences and n their count; ci90 = z90 * stdev / sqrt(n), and epCi90 the same for ep. The engine adds iterations to a stat until epCi90 is at or under precision.epCi90Target or its top-up passes run out.
method.fight: Every tree sims the Go test suites' default fight: full raid, party and individual buffs, full debuffs, one level 63 target, 180 s. Each tree records the values under baseline.buffs and baseline.encounter.
notes: identicalToBaseline marks a stat whose every probe iteration matched the baseline exactly: a measured 0. The engine returns no sample count for it, so n is the probe's pairs.
A weight of 0 for StatHitRating or StatExpertiseRating can also mean the baseline is at the cap.
The gear of every baseline is in baseline.player.equipment as the item and enchant ids simmed.
This file is weights-60.json with two additions from a second pass (each tree's passB block), every other value copied over unchanged.

weights.StatHitRating.below and weights.StatExpertiseRating.below: the weight of one step down from offset (a rating below the baseline, 0 for the baseline itself), paired with the run at offset as the engine pairs its runs, and run to the same interval. offset is below 0 where the baseline sits over a hit cap: the tree's belowCap block names the attack kinds, their caps and the hit at both ends of the step. The ep divides by the reference stat's weight measured again in the same pass (belowCap.reference).

Tank trees: weights[stat].tps, .dtps and .tmi, each with its own n and interval. tps divides by the reference stat's threat weight, dtps and tmi by StatArmor's, with the sign kept. The tankMetrics block gives the setup, the references, the worst intervals and the iteration cap, and replaces the first pass's tank block. Their weights[stat].dps stays the first pass's.

belowCap.rule: The step runs from offset down by one step. Hit is stepped down from the baseline until the top of the step is at or below the cap of every attack kind in channels: the miss of special attacks (the lower of the two hands when dual wielding, without the dual-wield penalty of auto attacks), of ranged attacks, or of spells, from the engine's attack table against the target. Expertise is stepped the same way against the target's dodge, and its parry when the player stands in front.

tankMetrics.setupFollowed: sim/core/test_generators.go, defaultPlayerAndRaid: a config with IsTank names the player in raid.Tanks, and the suite's single target, core.NewDefaultTarget() of sim/core/test_utils.go (level 63, 2601 minimum base damage, 2.0 s swing, parry haste, crushing blows), attacks it. That is how sim/warrior/protection/protection_test.go, sim/paladin/protection/protection_test.go and sim/druid/feralbear/feralbear_test.go set up their tank. The player stands in front of the target and carries the UI's healing model, without which the engine counts no TMI. sim/druid/feralbear/ep_test.go, the engine's one tank stat weight test, uses a harder-hitting target of 6000 minimum base damage; it is not followed, so that the three tanks and the first pass share one fight.
tankMetrics.signs: ep keeps the sign of weight over reference weight. Armor lowers damage taken and TMI, so a positive dtps or tmi ep lowers them as armor does, and a negative one raises them.

tmiAccountsForHealth.how: The engine's TMI (sim/core/metrics_aggregator.go calculateTMI) weighs each hit taken as its damage over the tank's maximum health (sim/core/health.go RemoveHealth), sums those over 6 s windows (the healing model's burst window) and takes 10 ln(mean e^(10 x window sum)). Stamina raises maximum health, so it lowers TMI while it leaves damage taken alone. TMI is counted only for a tanking player with a healing model.

tankMetrics.setupFollowed: sim/core/test_generators.go, defaultPlayerAndRaid: a config with IsTank names the player in raid.Tanks, and the suite's single target, core.NewDefaultTarget() of sim/core/test_utils.go (level 63, 2601 minimum base damage, 2.0 s swing, parry haste, crushing blows), attacks it. That is how sim/warrior/protection/protection_test.go, sim/paladin/protection/protection_test.go and sim/druid/feralbear/feralbear_test.go set up their tank. The player stands in front of the target and carries the UI's healing model, without which the engine counts no TMI. sim/druid/feralbear/ep_test.go, the engine's one tank stat weight test, uses a harder-hitting target of 6000 minimum base damage; it is not followed, so that the three tanks and the first pass share one fight.
tankMetrics.signs: ep keeps the sign of weight over reference weight. Armor lowers damage taken and TMI, so a positive dtps or tmi ep lowers them as armor does, and a negative one raises them.

tmiAccountsForHealth.how: The engine's TMI (sim/core/metrics_aggregator.go calculateTMI) weighs each hit taken as its damage over the tank's maximum health (sim/core/health.go RemoveHealth), sums those over 6 s windows (the healing model's burst window) and takes 10 ln(mean e^(10 x window sum)). Stamina raises maximum health, so it lowers TMI while it leaves damage taken alone. TMI is counted only for a tanking player with a healing model.
